summary_table.subtitle: CA maternity spend is being moved by a small number of very high-cost deliveries

rows.delivery_reimbursement: Bundled globally; only partial-care delivery CPTs separate; primary paid 100%, additional newborn/vaginal deliveries 50%.
rows.cesarean_modifier_rules: Document obstetric package level; for multiples, report diagnosis and code each vaginal newborn, cesarean once.

rows.delivery_reimbursement: Usually bundled globally; delivery-only reimbursed selectively, with additional vaginal births paid at reduced rates.
rows.cesarean_modifier_rules: Modifier 22 for multiple-birth cesareans requires documentation; reimbursement is reviewed case-by-case.

rows.delivery_reimbursement: United Health bundles routine vaginal delivery services; separate payment only with specified itemization/documented extra work.
rows.cesarean_modifier_rules: Modifier 22 allowed for third/fourth-degree lacerations with supporting medical record documentation.

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Routine obstetric delivery services are reimbursed under global, delivery-only, or delivery/postpartum codes depending on services provided. Single vaginal delivery is paid at full allowance. Multiple vaginal deliveries allow the first delivery at full allowance and additional deliveries at 50% with modifier 59. Multiple cesarean deliveries do not receive extra reimbursement unless modifier 22 is supported by documentation. Combined vaginal and cesarean deliveries follow separate sequencing rules. Delivery-related services such as augmentation of labor, amniotomy, vacuum extraction, and prolonged services are bundled or not separately reimbursed.

Routine vaginal delivery claims are bundled into the global maternity/obstetric package. Delivery-related inpatient care, labor checks, induction, and short delivery admissions are not separately reimbursed unless the claim is billed with a partial-care delivery-only or delivery-plus-postpartum CPT code.

Multiple-birth vaginal deliveries are paid at 100% for the primary procedure and 50% for each secondary delivery when a multiple gestation diagnosis is on the claim and at least one delivery is vaginal.

pairing_conditions: at least one delivery is vaginal
vaginal delivery followed by cesarean delivery

reimbursement_policies.evidence: The policy does not cite the requested DRG, but it is on-topic for maternity delivery claims. For multiple births delivered vaginally, reimbursement is allowed when billed with modifier 59, and each subsequent vaginal delivery is reimbursed at 50% of the allowance. If a combined-delivery method includes a cesarean delivery, modifier 22 and documentation review apply to the cesarean service.

utilization_limits: 50% allowance for each subsequent vaginal delivery

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: Obstetrical Policy, Professional - Reimbursement Policy - UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange
reimbursement_policies.evidence: Vaginal delivery-related OB services are generally bundled into delivery packages, with separate billing allowed only under specified itemization rules. Routine labor and delivery components are included, while increased procedural work may qualify for additional payment when properly documented.

This inpatient readmissions policy excludes obstetrical deliveries from separate readmission reimbursement rules, so maternity delivery admissions are generally outside the readmission bundling standard.

state_specific_rules: NC: pregnancy, childbirth and puerperium excluded
WA: obstetrical readmissions for birth after antepartum admission excluded

reimbursement_policies.evidence: This policy is mainly about sterilization reimbursement, but it affects maternity claims when sterilization is performed with a delivery. Sterilization is allowed only when consent and timing requirements are met, and multiple surgery rules apply when done with delivery. Tennessee Medicaid excludes facility reimbursement for sterilization performed with vaginal delivery under DRG methodology.

utilization_limits: 72-hour minimum for premature delivery or emergency abdominal surgery
state_specific_rules: TN: no facility reimbursement for sterilization with vaginal delivery under DRG methodology
IN: consent not required for illness, prior sterility, or unilateral procedure with documentation
IA: premature delivery consent must be at least 30 days before expected delivery date
MD: consent form not required with claims processing
VA: no consent form or waiting period for surgery that results in sterilization
WA: 30-day waiting period may be waived at delivery if eligibility and other criteria are met
WV: 30-day requirement waived and consent form not required with claims
exemptions: Indiana documentation exception for prior sterility, illness, injury, or unilateral procedure
West Virginia claims processing without consent form
Maryland claims processing without consent form

recommended_action.description:
Recommendation 1: For Commercial obstetrical claims in this California pattern, limit CPT 59514, 59515, 59620, and 59622 to single gestation and the same date of service/delivery confinement; when all deliveries are cesarean section, the cesarean code should be billed once, with modifier 22 reserved for documented exceptions, and multiple gestation excluded from this edit. Apply to California. Exempt: multiple gestation. Peer: Cigna and United Health both enforce single-gestation controls on obstetrical delivery CPTs and require modifier 22 for exceptional delivery claims..

Recommendation 2: In California, require modifier 59 on the same claim line for multiple births or combined vaginal and cesarean delivery scenarios, and reimburse each subsequent vaginal delivery at 50%; keep this narrow exception structure as the Commercial rule effective 01/01/2021 with no California changes effective 01/01/2026. Apply to California. Peer: Elevance and United Health both require obstetrical claims to distinguish separately payable services with modifier 59; Elevance further caps each subsequent vaginal delivery at 50% in multiple-birth cases..
